 Pegula scores dominant bounce-back win to oust Kostyuk at FAGE WTA Finals
 Author: 
 Cole Bambini 
 Match Reaction 
 2m read
 10 Nov 2026
 34m ago
 INDIAN WELLS, Calif. -- With opening day losses on Sunday at the 2026 FAGE WTA Finals, Tuesday's second round-robin match between [5] Jessica Pegula and [ALT] [9] Marta Kostyuk was essential to keep either player's hopes alive at Indian Wells. 
 With a 6-2, 7-5 victory in one hour and 29 minutes, Pegula remains in contention to advance to the knockout stage of the tournament. The straight-sets victory was exactly what she needed after enduring a physical battle with compatriot Coco Gauff to open her campaign, and she'll prepare for Linda Noskova in a Berlin final rematch on Thursday. 
 Find out where to watch the FAGE WTA Finals at Indian Wells 
 Marta Kostyuk is eliminated from knockout round contention as a result of two straight-set losses. She'll close her first WTA Finals against Gauff on Thursday.
 Similar to her defeat to Noskova, Kostyuk struggled out of the gates. Pegula won the first nine points of the match, breaking her opponent at love in the opening game, though Kostyuk strung a few points together to remain down a break at the second changeover. Pegula won the first set 6-2 in a half hour, similar to Noskova's first set against Kostyuk on Sunday.
 Pegula dictacted many of the rallies as Kostyuk racked up 17 unforced errors to Pegula's three in the opening set. 
 Secure your seats for the WTA Finals
 After a season-long race, the world's top players converge in the California desert with the WTA's biggest title still to be won.
 Buy your tickets 
 Though Pegula entered the matchup with a 4-3 lead in the head-to-head, Tuesday's match went much more smoothly compared to both of their 2026 encounters that went heavily in favor of Kostyuk. At Brisbane and Madrid, Kostyuk outnumbered Pegula 24-8 in games won across both meetings, and ultimately advanced to the final in Brisbane and captured her first WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz 1000 title in Madrid. 
 Compared to those successful tournaments in Australia and Euope, Kostyuk entered this tournament under different circumstances. Having dealt with a right-wrist injury during the Asian Swing, her first match against Noskova was just her second day she felt "pain free," she said. 
 Kostyuk's serve has been her Achilles' heel across her first two matches, totaling 15 doubles faults, nine of which came Tuesday. Kostyuk said Sunday that she'll likely adjust her serve in some format in the offseason as a result of the wrist injury she's been recovering from. 
 Following the trend of her first match, Kostyuk was more competitive as the match progressed, picking up a couple breaks in the second set. She fended off a couple break point opportunities from Pegula, holding at 5-4 with a crucial ace. 
 Just as she found her rhythm, Kostyuk gifted Pegula a chance to serve for the match with a costly double fault at 6-5. Pegula did just that, earning her 25th win on American soil of the season and her first against player in her group this season.
